newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council concerned over Angola peace delays.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council concerned over Angola peace delays.

text.p: The United Nations Security Council, echoing a report by Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, expressed concern on Wednesday about lack of progress in carrying out a two-year-old peace plan for Angola, particularly blaming former UNITA rebels.

In a statement to reporters after closed-door consultations, council President Gerardo Martinez Blanco of Honduras said the council was "extremely concerned about the lack of significant progress in the peace process in Angola and the delays in the implementation of the Lusaka Protocol."
He was referring to a November 1994 agreement ending nearly two decades of civil war between the Angolan government and the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA).
"The council also expresses its concern over UNITA's lack of cooperation to the Angolan peace efforts," Martinez Blanco added.
His statement commended the efforts of the U.N. secretary-general's special representative for Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye of Mali, who had earlier briefed the council privately.

Boutros-Ghali, in a written report to the council on Monday, expressed serious concern over continuing delays, particularly by UNITA, in carrying out the Angola peace accord and recommended only a two-month renewal of the 7,264-member U.N. operation there.
The present three-month mandate of the force, currently the biggest U.N. peacekeeping operation, expires Friday, when the council is expected to approve a two-month renewal.
The council is also due to meet on Thursday to debate the Angola situation at the request of the foreign ministers of Angola, Botswana, Mozambique, South Africa and Zimbabwe.
